question: Can pure-decode width2 round robin remove the cap16 group boundary cost without moving a larger delay onto held requests?
hypothesis: C16/topk8 gives at most one expert group per layer for two decode rows. Extra model calls and held-request intervals are charged; structural savings alone do not imply faster requests.
event: Common token prefix; inject third request after four incumbent outputs; switch to expert and arm chunk. RR has no action during two-request prefix or mixed prefill.
costs: Same instrumentation, all six warmup sequences, episode trace flush and parent/engine cycle. Actual peak memory retained; validation after capture is outside request wall.
prestate: Source-ID normalized logical metadata including output tokens, positions, KV counts and pager slots/LRU. Physical KV IDs retained separately; no KV tensor equality claim.
scope: Eight same-engine episodes on the already viewed source triplet. Artificial OLMoE expert capacity; natural policy-specific generation. Not an independent holdout, quality result, production tail estimate, true over-HBM model or SLO result.
stops: Foreign GPU process or failed query; native source mismatch; incomplete or changed task; budget restoration/held state/rotation failure; observed union/group violation. Retain all attempts and do not select favorable cells.
comparison: Compare rr32 against static32 matched no-action arm and independently selected static16 wall/static8 old-pause baselines. Show both blocks, all-request costs and same-arm repeat drift. No observed maximum used as a population noise bound.
continuation: If full-request gains survive all three simple baselines, validate fresh requests and clock arrivals with this exact action. Otherwise decompose the necessary extra-call/held-wait cost; do not tune a sequence of width thresholds or kill the problem family.
ordering: Declared static8/static16/static32/rr32 then reverse; two observations per arm, not independent randomized blocks.
action: Only when exactly three pure decode requests are ready and both waiting queues empty: temporarily set native schedule token budget64 to2, run native schedule, validate held request RUNNING/KV/computed unchanged, rotate running order by2, restore budget64. No eviction or fixed future routes.
fairness: While the three-request pure-decode condition persists, no request is held on consecutive nonempty calls. This is a step bound, not a wall-time guarantee.
